summaries.Romania: Romania faces political instability as President Nicușor Dan prepares to nominate a new premier amid disputes over judicial reforms and EU compliance, while government agencies work to secure PNRR funding. Security concerns escalate with repeated Russian drone incursions and sabotage allegations across Europe.
summaries.Healthcare: Healthcare innovation accelerates with AI-driven oncology platforms, remote patient monitoring expansions, and significant funding rounds, while drug pricing negotiations and substance abuse prevention initiatives reshape the healthcare landscape. Major systems like McKesson face cybersecurity threats affecting patient data security.
summaries.Tech: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro launches next week with GPU upgrades and higher memory costs, while Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face for $12.9B signals consolidation in AI infrastructure. Critical security breaches affecting millions of driver's licenses and a Google antitrust ruling reshape the tech regulatory environment.

items.title: Nvidia confirms it will buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion
items.snippet: Nvidia said Hugging Face hosts over 3 million models and is used by over 18 million developers.
items.line: Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B, consolidating control over open-source AI model infrastructure used by 18M developers.

items.title: Oncology company Thyme Care raises $125M, backed by Morgan Health, Humana and CVS Health Ventures
items.snippet: Thyme Care landed a series E financing round of more than $125 million backed by strategic payers and providers as it aims to expand beyond cancer care navigation.

items.title: McKesson confirms cybersecurity incident as hackers claim millions of patient records stolen
items.snippet: Healthcare giant McKesson Corporation confirmed on Friday that it was investigating a cybersecurity incident tied to third-party applications that led to unauthorized access and theft of data.
items.line: McKesson confirms cybersecurity breach compromising millions of patient records through third-party applications, raising healthcare data security concerns.

items.title: Google spared from ad-business breakup, but judge orders changes to how it operates
items.snippet: Google has dodged an effort to break up its ad business, but a judge said Wednesday that the company will need to adjust its business to benefit competitors.
items.line: Judge orders Google to modify ad business operations rather than forced breakup, setting precedent for tech antitrust enforcement without divestiture.
